title: US Senate panel votes to hold Fauci in contempt over COVID hearing

Topic:World Politics

Anthony Fauci refused to answer questions at a hearing focused on his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. (Reuters: Nathan Howard)

A US Senate committee has voted to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress over his refusal to answer questions at a hearing about COVID.

Dr Fauci said he had good reason to fear the possibility of criminal charges due to Republicans' determination to see him "end up, in his words, quote, behind bars, unquote".

Dr Fauci will now be referred to the US Attorney's Office in Washington, which will make a decision on whether or not to investigate or potentially attempt to prosecute the doctor for contempt.

A US Senate committee has voted to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress and refer him to the Department of Justice for potential prosecution over his refusal to answer questions at a hearing focused on his handling of the COVID pandemic.

Dr Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination more than 100 times when he appeared before the US Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs last week.

Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky, the Republican committee chairman, has said that the constitutional privilege did not apply to Dr Fauci, who last year received a pardon from former president Joe Biden and thus did not have to worry about the threat of prosecution.

The former top US infectious disease expert declines to answer questions at a Republican-led Senate hearing, labelling it an "unhinged" campaign to see him imprisoned.

But Dr Fauci, in a statement issued before the hearing, said he had good reason to fear the possibility of criminal charges given what he said was Senator Paul's determination "to get me to say something, anything, that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, behind bars, unquote".

"Dr Fauci faced no risk of federal prosecution," Senator Paul said at the outset of a hearing.

"All he had to do was tell the truth."

The senator noted that Thursday's vote had nothing to do with Dr Fauci's policies, opinions or anything he has said in previous congressional appearances.

Instead, the senator said: "We are voting on whether a witness who has received the benefit of a sweeping pardon can be ordered by this committee to answer questions and then defy that order without consequence."

CNN later reported that Senator Paul would refer Dr Fauci to the Justice Department.

Rand Paul said the vote was not about Dr Fauci's policies or opinions.  (Reuters: Nathan Howard)

Dr Fauci's pardon from Mr Biden covered acts from 2014 through the January 2025 day it was issued.

It does not shield Dr Fauci from state-level prosecutions or from investigations into any testimony that he did give that politicians thought was false.

Dr Fauci will now be referred to the US Attorney's Office in Washington, which would make a decision on whether or not to investigate or potentially attempt to prosecute the doctor for contempt.

Senator Paul, who has previously sent referrals on Dr Fauci on his own, acknowledged on Wednesday, local time, that contempt resolutions have often gone through the full Senate but said he did not "want to waste time" moving the matter to a vote of the full Senate, where it would be unlikely to muster the required 60 votes needed to advance.

"We still might come to the floor," he said. "But at this point, the first thing we will do is we will send it over as a recommendation from our committee, if it passes."
